mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which compresses earnings for industrial firms and drags the S&P 500 lower over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during three consecutive months of INDPRO declines exceeding -0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and inflation, which increases real discount rates and erodes real corporate earnings, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive correlation between monthly changes in real personal income (proxied by GDPC1 growth) and monthly changes in the S&P 500 over the preceding 12 months implies that continued income growth will sustain equity demand, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 grows month-over-month, S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their 12-month averages signals a labor market normalization after a downturn, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and UNRATE both exceed 12-month averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and UNRATE exceed their 12-month averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average, combined with a concurrent rise in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1), signals robust housing demand and broader consumption strength, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month average AND GDPC1 > 12-month average in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both HOUST and GDPC1 exceed their 12-month averages in the same month.
